title: Catalytic Scavenging of Plant Reactive Oxygen Species In Vivo by Anionic Cerium Oxide Nanoparticles
protocol: Sow A. thaliana seeds in 5 cm x 5 cm disposable pots filled with standard soil mix.
Place 32 pots into a plastic tray filled with water (~0.5 cm depth).
Transfer the plastic tray with plants into a plant growth chamber.
Set the growth chamber settings to 200 µmol/ms PAR, 24 ± 1 °C day and 21 ± 1 °C night, 60% humidity, and a 14/10 h light regime.
Thin each pot to leave only one individual plant after one week of germination.
Water the pots by pouring tap water directly on the plastic tray once every two days.
Grow the plants for four weeks.
Weigh 1.08 g of cerium (III) nitrate and dissolve it in 2.5 mL of molecular biology grade water in a 50 mL conical tube.
Weigh 4.5 g of poly(acrylic) acid and dissolve it in 5 mL of molecular biology grade water in a 50 mL conical tube.
Mix the two solutions thoroughly at 2,000 rpm for 15 min using a digital vortex mixer.
Transfer 15 mL of ammonium hydroxide solution (7.2 M) to a 50 mL glass beaker.
While stirring at 500 rpm, add the mixture dropwise to the ammonium hydroxide solution.
Stir the mixture at 500 rpm at room temperature for 24 hr in a fume hood.
Cover the beaker with a piece of paper.
Centrifuge the solution in a 50 mL conical tube at 3,900 x g for 1 hour.
Transfer 22.5 mL of supernatant into three 15 mL 10 kDa filters.
Fill the remainder of each filter with molecular grade water to reach a total dilution of 45 mL.
Centrifuge the supernatant solution through a 15 mL 10 kDa filter at 3,900 x g for 15 minutes.
Repeat centrifugation step at least six times.
Measure absorbance of eluent in each cycle from 220-700 nm.
Take collected PNC solution into a 5 mL syringe.
Filter the PNC solution through a 20 nm pore size syringe filter.
Collect filtered PNC solution in a 50 mL conical tube.
Measure absorbance of diluted final PNC solution from 220-700 nm.
Calculate PNC concentration using Beer-Lambert's law: A = εCL.
Measure hydrodynamic diameter and zeta potential of PNC using a particle size and zeta potential analyzer.
Store final PNC solution in refrigerator (4 °C).
Mix 0.4 mL of 5 mM PNC with 3.6 mL molecular biology grade water in a 20 mL glass vial and stir at 500 rpm.
Add 24 µL DiI dye solution to 176 µL DMSO to make the dye solution.
Add DiI dye dropwise to the PNC solution, stirring at 1,000 rpm for 1 min at ambient temperature.
Transfer resulting mixture into a 15 mL 10 kDa filter and fill tube with molecular biology grade water to total dilution of 15 mL.
Purify DiI-labeled PNC (DiI-PNC) solution from DMSO using a benchtop centrifugation with the 15 mL 10 kDa filter at 3,900 x g for 5 min.
Repeat purification step at least five times.
Filter the final DiI-PNC solutions through a 20 nm pore size syringe filter.
Measure the absorbance of the final DiI-PNC solution by UV-VIS spectrophotometry.
Calculate its concentration according to Beer-Lambert's law.
Store the filtered and measured DiI-PNC solution in a refrigerator at 4 °C for further use.
Add 0.1 mL of infiltration buffer (100 mM TES, 100 mM MgCl2, pH 7.5) into 0.9 mL of 0.5 mM PNC or DiI-PNC solution and vortex it.
Use a solution of 10 mM TES infiltration buffer as a negative control.
Transfer 0.2 mL of the PNC or DiI-PNC infiltration solution to a 1 mL sterile needleless syringe.
Tap the syringe to remove any possible air bubbles.
Retrieve the plant from the growth chamber just before infiltration with nanoparticles to avoid possible stomata closure under room light conditions.
Measure the chlorophyll content from A. thaliana leaves using a chlorophyll meter.
Choose A. thaliana leaves with similar chlorophyll content for the infiltration experiment.
Infiltrate the chosen leaves slowly with the recently prepared PNC or DiI-PNC solution by gently pressing the tip of the needleless syringe against the bottom of the leaf lamina (abaxial side).
Depress the plunger to infiltrate the leaf.
Gently wipe off the excess solution that remains on the surface of leaf lamina using a delicate task wiper and label the plant.
Use new delicate task wipes for each group of leaves.
Keep the infiltrated A. thaliana plants on the bench for leaf adaptation and incubation with PNC or DiI-PNC for 3 h.
Roll a pea-size amount of observation gel to about a 1 cm radius.
Spread the rolled gel out until it is 1 mm thin on a glass slide.
Cut out a circular section at the center of the observation gel using a cork borer (diameter 0.3 cm).
Fill the cut well entirely with perfluorodecalin for deeper and better confocal imaging resolution in leaf tissues.
Collect leaf discs from adapted DiI-PNC infiltrated A. thaliana plants using a cork borer (diameter 0.2 cm).
Mount the leaf disc in the PFD filled well, facing the infiltrated side of the leaf up.
Place a square coverslip on top of the leaf disc and gently press evenly to seal it with the observation gel well.
Drop two to three drops of ddH2O on the top of the 40X objective lens.
Place the prepared DiI-PNC infiltrated leaf sample slide on top of the inverted 40X objective lens.
Ensure the coverslip side contacts the ddH2O on the lens without touching the glass slide directly.
Find a region of interest in the sample using either laser light or bright field.
Start the microscope software and turn on the Argon laser (set at 20%).
Set the pinhole to collect an optical slice less than 2 µm with a line average of 4.
Image the sample with confocal microscopy settings: 514 nm laser excitation (30 %); Z-Stack section thickness: 2 µm; PMT1: 550-615 nm for DiI-PNC imaging; PMT2: 700-800 nm for chloroplast imaging.
Take representative confocal images of leaf samples from different individuals, a minimum of three biological replicates.
Prepare 25 µM 2',7'-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate (H2DCFDA) in TES infiltration buffer (pH 7.5).
Prepare 10 µM dihydroethidium (DHE) in TES infiltration buffer (pH 7.5).
Use a cork borer to collect leaf discs from the adapted PNC infiltrated A. thaliana plants.
Make three to four holes on each leaf disc using the sharp tip of forceps.
Transfer the leaf discs to microcentrifuge tubes with H2DCFDA and incubate under darkness for 30 min.
Transfer the leaf discs to microcentrifuge tubes with DHE and incubate under darkness for 30 min.
Rinse the leaf discs with ddH2O three times after incubation.
Mount the rinsed leaf discs into glass slides with observation gel.
Place the slide on the confocal microscope and manually focus on mesophyll cells.
Expose the leaf discs to UV-A (405 nm) laser for 3 min to generate ROS.
Record the ROS signal intensity change in time-series ("xyt") per leaf disc.
Image the leaf disc using a 40X water objective, 496 nm laser excitation, PMT1: 500-600 nm and PMT2: 700-800 nm settings.
Conduct CAT (catalase) mimetic activity of synthesized PNC in vitro following previous publications' methods.
Add 45.4 µL of 1x TES infiltration buffer, PNC (60 nM), and H2O2 (2 µM) into a well.
Gently mix the solution by pipetting.
Add 10-acetyl-3,7-dihydroxyphenoxazine (working concentration 100 µM) and horseradish peroxidase (HRP; working concentration 0.2 U/mL) to the well.
Gently mix again by pipetting.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min.
Wrap the plate with aluminum foil to avoid light during the incubation.
Prepare a negative control by using reaction buffer or water in place of H2O2.
Monitor absorbance at 560 nm with a plate reader after incubation periods of 0, 2, 5, 10, 20, and 30 minutes.
